correctness.rationale: For ν=d/2≥1 the annular Fourier amplitude equals (2π)^ν t^(−ν)[Jν(t)−r^νJν(rt)]. The Bessel recurrences give Eν′(t)=(4ν−2)t^(2ν−1)Jν−1(t)²≥0, with strictly positive integral on each interval (rt,t), so strict two-scale energy dominance holds for all t>0. At each boundary t=jν−1,k the scaled difference has the sign of Jν(t), giving alternating signs at consecutive brackets. At any root, dominance yields |Jν−1(t)|>r^ν|Jν−1(rt)|, forcing G′ nonzero with sign Jν−1, which cannot recur twice in one bracket. No first root occurs below jν−1,1 by the positive origin sign and derivative direction. The implicit-function theorem and compact-limit Bessel expansions prove analytic motion and limiting jν,k (r↓0), jν−1,k (r↑1), and bracket uniform N(t)=t/π+O_d(1). At d=1 the sine-cosine factorization classifies precisely the odd-numerator/even-denominator rational resonances with double zeros. Independent SciPy computation reproduced 28 bracket roots and derivative orientation (diagnostic, not proof).
residual_risks: Simplicity refers to radial Fourier *amplitude* zeros, not intensity, and no assertion is made for nonconcentric/nonradial shells or complex zeros.
